Tree Gating and Visualisation

cytoGateR authors

Source: vignettes/Tree_Gating_Visualisation.qmd

1 Overview

This vignette demonstrates an interpretable tree-gating workflow on one complete image from cytoGateR_example. A small two-lineage marker table keeps the build fast while exercising the same functions used by larger analyses.

library(cytoGateR)
data("cytoGateR_example", package = "cytoGateR")

image_ids <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(cytoGateR_example)$image_name
spe <- cytoGateR_example[, image_ids == image_ids[1L]]
spe

2 Define a lineage table

Each row defines a cell type using positive and negative protein markers. Marker columns are list-columns so that each cell type may use a different number of markers.

lineage_table <- data.frame(
  cell_type = c("Tcell", "Bcell"),
  pos_markers = I(list("CD3e", "CD20")),
  neg_markers = I(list("CD20", "CD3e"))
)
lineage_table
  cell_type pos_markers neg_markers
1     Tcell        CD3e        CD20
2     Bcell        CD20        CD3e

3 Fit tree-gating models

For package-build speed, the example limits each tree to one split. Larger analyses can increase max_depth and use more detailed marker definitions.

tree_result <- run_tree_gating(
  spe,
  lineage_table,
  assay_name = "exprs",
  max_depth = 1,
  min_cells = 100,
  min_score = 0.1,
  uncert_thresh = 0.25,
  workers = 1
)

The result contains the updated object, fitted trees, probability matrix, hard labels, and cleaned lineage table:

names(tree_result)
[1] "spe"           "trees"         "prob_mat"      "hard_label"

4 Inspect the fitted trees 

print_celltype_tree(tree_result$trees$Tcell)
[depth 0] CD3e > 1.565  (sep = 2.78, n = 4363)
 |- low
 |  [leaf] depth =1 n_cells =1492
 `- high
    [leaf] depth =1 n_cells =2871
plot_celltype_tree(tree_result$trees$Tcell)

5 Select high-confidence cells

apply_cutoff_labels() applies a cell-type-specific probability cutoff. A cell receives a reference label only when exactly one cell type passes its cutoff.

core_result <- apply_cutoff_labels(
  tree_result,
  cutoff_fn = function(x) stats::quantile(x, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
  label_col = "core_group",
  unknown_label = "Unknown"
)

table(SummarizedExperiment::colData(core_result$spe)$core_group)

  Bcell   Tcell Unknown
    219     219    3925

6 Visualise expression and annotations

Marker distributions help assess whether the selected markers separate the expected populations.

plot_marker_density(
  core_result$spe,
  marker = "CD3e",
  assay_name = "exprs",
  image_col = "image_name"
)

The gated labels can also be displayed in spatial coordinates:

plot_labelled_cells(
  core_result$spe,
  col_label = "core_group",
  image_col = "image_name"
)

7 Visualise stored full-workflow probabilities

The packaged object contains probabilities from the full ten-lineage demo workflow. These provide a richer example for probability visualisation without rerunning the complete model during vignette construction.

plot_probability_map(
  spe,
  cell_type = "Bcell",
  image_col = "image_name"
)
plot_label_counts(
  spe,
  label_col = "knn_label"
)
